newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.5 percent in November.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.5 percent in November.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.5 percent in November after rising a revised 0.4 percent (0.3 percent) in October, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast real GDP to rise 0.4 percent in November.
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.
Statistics Canada said a rebound in production of motor vehicles and parts, following the October strike at General Motors Corp's Canadian unit, accounted for half of the November gains.
"As well, consumers appear to be shaking their wariness as retail sales rose firmly for a second consecutive month and strong housing sales boosted real estate and legal services," the agency said.
However, wholesalers recorded lower sales and activity in the mining and construction sectors also slowed down.
(For more information from Statistics Canada contact Michel Girard, Industry Measures and Analysis Division, at 613-951-9145).
